hints: Every cell is entered either from above or from the left. If you already know the cheapest cost to reach those two, what is the cheapest cost to reach this one?
2D grid DP: cost[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(cost[r−1][c], cost[r][c−1]), with only one option on the first row and column. A single row array is enough.

1. dp = array of width cols.
  2. For each row r, for each column c: if r == 0 and c == 0, dp[c] = grid[0][0].
  3. Else from = min of dp[c] (above, if r > 0) and dp[c−1] (left, if c > 0); dp[c] = grid[r][c] + from.
  4. Return dp[cols−1].

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every right/down path and add up its cells.

explain: Sample 1 grid [[1,4,2],[2,8,1],[5,1,3]]. Row 0: [1,5,7]. Row 1: [3, 8+min(5,3)=11, 1+min(7,11)=8]. Row 2: [8, 1+min(11,8)=9, 3+min(8,9)=11]. Answer 11. The cheapest way into a cell must come through the cheapest way into one of its two neighbours, which is why taking the min is safe. The first row and column only have one way in, so handle them without the min.
recognize: Min-cost path from top-left to bottom-right moving right/down → grid DP taking min of top and left.
